subject: Re: Sequencing UK Addendum + TIA steps for NovaPharm
messages:
From: Euan McLeod <euan.mcleod@novapharm.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: NovaPharm Legal <legal@novapharm.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: UK Addendum / TIA sequencing — ask and attachments

Monica,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is a filled TIA worksheet and our high-level carve-out questions. Legal have highlighted two items they want clarified BEFORE signing the UK Addendum:

- Whether Redwood can provide onshore fallback for logging/escrow (we need explicit statement of retention locality).
- Subprocessor disclosure cadence — we require a 30-day notice for onboarding EU/UK subprocessors tied to TIA scope.

Can you propose a minimal sequencing plan that keeps our go-live timeline (target: 2026-10-15) while not delaying signature? If you need additional info from engineering or compliance, loop them in.

Best,
Euan
Business Contracts — NovaPharm

Attachments: NovaPharm_TIA_worksheet.xlsx

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Euan McLeod <euan.mcleod@novapharm.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: UK Addendum / TIA sequencing — proposed approach

Euan — thanks for the worksheet. High level response and proposed sequencing below. I copied our infra and legal leads for technical and timeline confirmation.

Proposed sequencing (minimal-signature-first approach):
1) Sign UK Addendum + DPA baseline (explicitly note TIA in schedule) — proceed to signature with a defined follow-up window for detailed TIA artifacts (30 days).
2) Redwood to provide interim onshore fallback statement (operational commitment) + schedule for onshore log escrow implementation as a tech deliverable (within 45 days post-signature).
3) Subprocessor cadence: we will commit to 30-day notice for new EU/UK subprocessors and provide the current subprocessor CSV in the DPA exhibit.
4) Finalize TIA artifacts (detailed safeguards, sampling plan) within the 30-day window; if gaps remain, add a narrow operational milestone plan rather than blocking signature.

Open questions for our side:
- Kimber: can you confirm the feasibility of a 45-day target for onshore fallback logging (minimal viable escrow)?
- Jonas: can legal accept signature with the timeline binding to deliverables rather than full artifact delivery upfront?

If that works, I suggest we prepare a short amendment language snippet that NovaPharm can sign to capture the timeline obligations.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Head of Trust Programs — Redwood Inference
(Attachments: redwood_dpa_draft_v3.docx)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Euan McLeod <euan.mcleod@novapharm.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T15:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: UK Addendum / TIA sequencing — infra feasibility notes

Monica / Jonas / Euan,

Quick infra check: the proposed 45-day window for a minimal onshore fallback (logs escrow + retention policy) is feasible if we scope it as:
- Short-term: export logs to a UK region object store with retention tagging (read-only access for auditors) — dev sprint + infra provisioning ~3 weeks.
- Mid-term: formalize escrow process and KMS separation for the UK escrow bucket — additional 2 weeks (key rotation and access control).

Constraints / caveats:
- This will be a focused operational control, not a full data residency re-architecture. Some telemetry may still route through EU edge nodes; we will document the exact transfer pathways in the TIA artifacts.
- Subprocessor notice: we can provide programmatic notifications (API webhook + daily CSV) but cannot retroactively delay a subprocessor already in the pipeline; 30-day notice is doable for new ones going forward.

I'll prepare a short technical statement (1 page) describing the fallback implementation and the deliverable acceptance criteria.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Infrastructure Security — Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Euan McLeod <euan.mcleod@novapharm.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: UK Addendum / TIA sequencing — legal signoff path

Euan / Monica,

Thanks — from a legal execution perspective we are comfortable with the minimal-signature-first approach provided we have:
- A short amendment clause in the UK Addendum that captures the delivery milestones (30/45-day buckets) and an explicit cure path if items are missed.
- A HubSpot deal note tying acceptance signoff to the acceptance of the technical statement and the completed TIA artifact checklist.

Action items I propose:
1) Redwood to share amendment draft and Kim's 1-page technical fallback statement by 2026-09-02 EOD.
2) NovaPharm legal to confirm acceptance or raise maximum two redlines to the amendment within 48 hours of receipt.
3) Execute Addendum + Amendment via DocuSign; follow with delivery sprints.

If NovaPharm needs a longer review period, tell us now — it will affect the 10/15 go-live.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Sr. Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: Euan McLeod <euan.mcleod@novapharm.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: UK Addendum / TIA sequencing — confirm next steps

Team — thanks for the clear path. NovaPharm legal have asked for two small clarifications which should be fast:
1) Add explicit language that the 30-day TIA window can be extended by mutual written agreement (to avoid inadvertent breaches).
2) Confirm that the subprocessor CSV will include change-date metadata for each entry.

If you can include those in the amendment draft, we can review and aim to sign by 2026-09-04. We also need the current subprocessor CSV attached to the DPA exhibit prior to signature.

Euan
